apple apple scab.summary: Venturia inaequalis fungus causing olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit.
do_now: Remove and bin fallen and infected leaves
Avoid wetting the foliage when watering
organic: Sulfur or copper fungicide at bud break
chemical: Captan or myclobutanil per label
Repeat during wet spring weather
prevent: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn

apple black rot.summary: Botryosphaeria fungus causing frog-eye leaf spots, cankers, and rotting fruit.
do_now: Cut out cankered branches well below the lesion
Remove mummified fruit from the tree
chemical: Captan or thiophanate-methyl per label
prevent: Remove nearby wild or neglected apples

apple cedar apple rust.summary: Gymnosporangium rust needing both apple and juniper hosts; bright orange leaf spots.
do_now: Remove nearby juniper galls if possible
organic: Sulfur spray from pink bud through early summer
chemical: Myclobutanil at bud break, repeat per label

prevent: Water at the base, not the leaves

cherry including sour powdery mildew.summary: White powdery fungal growth on leaves and shoots, common in warm, humid conditions.
do_now: Remove and bin the worst affected leaves
organic: Neem oil weekly on new growth
chemical: Myclobutanil or trifloxystrobin per label

corn maize cercospora leaf spot gray lea.summary: Cercospora fungus causing long rectangular gray-to-tan lesions between leaf veins.
do_now: Avoid working in the field when wet
chemical: Strobilurin or triazole fungicide at first sign

corn maize common rust.summary: Puccinia sorghi causing small cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
organic: Sulfur or copper fungicide if severe
chemical: Triazole fungicide if infection is early and heavy

corn maize northern leaf blight.summary: Exserohilum turcicum causing long cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.
organic: Copper fungicide early in the season
chemical: Strobilurin or triazole fungicide around tasseling

grape black rot.summary: Guignardia bidwellii causing tan leaf spots and shriveled black 'mummy' berries.
do_now: Remove all mummified berries and infected leaves
Bin, do not compost, the debris
organic: Copper or sulfur from bud break
chemical: Myclobutanil or mancozeb from early shoot growth

grape esca black measles.summary: A trunk-disease complex causing tiger-stripe leaves and spotted berries; often fatal to vines.
do_now: Prune out dead spurs and cordons in dry weather
organic: Protect large pruning wounds with paste
chemical: No reliable cure; manage by removing infected wood

grape leaf blight isariopsis leaf spot.summary: Pseudocercospora causing dark angular leaf spots, mostly late season.
chemical: Mancozeb or a strobilurin per label

orange haunglongbing citrus greening.summary: HLB, spread by the citrus psyllid, causing blotchy mottled leaves and bitter lopsided fruit. No cure.
do_now: Isolate and consider removing infected trees to protect others
organic: Neem or horticultural oil for psyllid control
chemical: Approved insecticides for psyllid management per local guidance

peach bacterial spot.summary: Xanthomonas causing angular purple-brown leaf spots that drop out, plus fruit cracking.
do_now: Remove severely spotted leaves and fruit
organic: Copper sprays at low rates (watch for phytotoxicity)
chemical: Oxytetracycline or copper per label during the season

pepper bell bacterial spot.summary: Xanthomonas causing small water-soaked spots that turn brown with yellow halos.
chemical: Copper-based bactericide per label

potato early blight.summary: Alternaria solani causing concentric-ring 'target' spots on older leaves.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb per label
prevent: Keep plants well fed and watered

potato late blight.summary: Phytophthora infestans causing fast-spreading dark water-soaked lesions; can destroy a crop in days.
do_now: Remove and bin infected plants immediately
organic: Copper fungicide preventively in cool wet weather
chemical: Mancozeb or chlorothalonil, or systemic products in outbreaks

squash powdery mildew.summary: White powdery patches on leaves and stems, spreading fast in warm, dry days with humid nights.
chemical: Sulfur or myclobutanil per label
prevent: Water at the base early in the day

strawberry leaf scorch.summary: Diplocarpon causing dark purple spots that merge, giving leaves a scorched look.
chemical: Captan or myclobutanil per label

prevent: Mulch to keep fruit off soil

tomato bacterial spot.summary: Xanthomonas causing small dark greasy spots on leaves and scabby fruit spots.
chemical: Copper bactericide per label

tomato early blight.summary: Alternaria causing concentric brown 'target' spots on lower leaves first.
do_now: Remove affected lower leaves and bin them
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb per label

tomato late blight.summary: Phytophthora infestans causing large greasy gray-brown blotches; can kill plants in days.
do_now: Remove and bin infected plants at once
organic: Copper fungicide preventively in cool, wet weather
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb; systemic products in outbreaks

tomato leaf mold.summary: Passalora fulva causing pale yellow patches above and olive mold below leaves; common in humid greenhouses.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb per label
prevent: Space plants and prune lower leaves

tomato septoria leaf spot.summary: Septoria causing many small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb per label

tomato spider mites two spotted spider m.summary: Tiny mites causing fine stippling, yellowing, and webbing on leaf undersides in hot, dry spells.
do_now: Spray leaf undersides with a strong jet of water
organic: Insecticidal soap or neem oil, repeat every 5-7 days
chemical: A labeled miticide (rotate modes of action)
prevent: Keep plants watered (mites love drought stress)

tomato target spot.summary: Corynespora causing brown spots with concentric rings on leaves and fruit.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or a strobilurin per label

tomato tomato yellow leaf curl virus.summary: Whitefly-spread virus causing upward leaf curling, yellowing, and stunted growth. No cure.
do_now: Remove and bin infected plants to protect others
organic: Neem oil and yellow sticky traps for whiteflies
chemical: Approved insecticides for whitefly control per local guidance

tomato tomato mosaic virus.summary: Highly contagious virus causing mottled light-and-dark leaves and distorted growth. No cure.
do_now: Wash hands and tools with soap after handling
organic: No spray cures a virus; focus on sanitation
chemical: None; manage by removal and hygiene
prevent: Do not use tobacco near plants
